title: Audit trail names the staff member and the distributorship, shows the reason and a before → after line, and can be narrowed by distributorship, action and staff member; the distributor detail names who asked for each support window
rootCause:
The four symptoms have one cause: apart from `admin.support.list` (and the replies of `admin.support.request/revoke`), no console read turns a platform administrator's id into a name, and the audit screen never uses the filters the service already has. All line numbers are on main 04c193e (DOS-106 merged), not b59bbf0.

1. **"Who" = "Distribution OS staff" on every row.**
   - The screen prints `word(row.actorRole)` in the column (frontend/admin-app/app/audit.tsx:79) and in the Sheet (:139). `word.platform_admin` is 'Distribution OS staff' (frontend/admin-app/src/strings.ts:380).
   - The service hard-codes `actorRole: 'platform_admin'` (backend/libs/core/src/modules/platform-admin/console.service.ts:295).
   - The wire row has no name: `PlatformAuditEntrySchema` (backend/libs/contracts/src/admin.ts:485-489) extends `AuditEntrySchema` (tenancy.ts:329-341) with `tenantId` and `tenantSlug` only.
   - The data is correct. Read-only SQL on dos_qa: 23 `platform_audit` rows, 3 distinct `admin_user_id`s; `dos_support_requester_names()` resolves all three ('Rohit Nair (Distribution OS)' = dos.admin, 'Anita Rao (Distribution OS support)' = dos.support, 'Platform support' = an rls.test fixture).
   - **"join users" would not work.** Console reads run under `withPlatform` (internals.ts:46) and `users_visible` (backend/libs/database/src/schema/tenancy.ts:157-163) admits only the actor or a member of `app.tenant_id`, which is empty for a console session. A join names the reader's own rows and returns null for a colleague's, exactly the two-actor case of the finding.
   - The sanctioned lookup exists: SECURITY DEFINER `dos_support_requester_names(text[])` (migrations/0037_support_requester_name.sql:22-32: pinned search_path, joins `platform_admins` with no `disabled_at` filter, EXECUTE granted to app_rw and app_worker, guarded by its DO block). It is used by `PlatformSupportService.requesterNames` (support.service.ts:221-232) and by a separate copy in tenancy/support.service.ts:227-236. docs/23 §10 row 13 (line 949) records this exact gap.

2. **No reason and no before/after on a row.**
   - The mapper sets `before: null, after: payload` (console.service.ts:299-300).
   - Every writer puts the facts in the payload:
     - tenants.service.ts:342-346 `{from,to,reason}` (suspend/reactivate).
     - subscriptions.service.ts:186-196 `{plan,status,amountPaise,billingInterval,from:{plan,status,amountPaise}}`; `from.status` is the column value 'trial', the top-level `status` the wire value 'trialing'.
     - support.service.ts:87-95 `{grantId,hours,scope,reason}` and :187-196 `{grantId,was,now,reason}`.
     - console.service.ts:182-184 (raw SQL) `{userId,username,reason}`.
     - tenants.service.ts:262-270 `tenant.onboarded` `{plan,slug,trialDays,ownerUserId}` through `insertPlatformAuditUnderSystem` (:382-392).
     - service/support-audit.interceptor.ts:71-81 `support.read` `{grantId,scope,method,route,outcome}`.
   - The Register's columns are action+time, slug, role word and entityType (audit.tsx:53-81). The Sheet dumps the payload as JSON under 'After', cut at 12 lines (:149-155).
   - The action words are out of step: strings.ts has keys for `tenant.created`, `support.revoked` and `support.approve`, none of which is written to `platform_audit` (`support.approve` goes to the tenant `audit_log`, tenancy/support.service.ts:146-157), and none for `tenant.onboarded` or `support.withdrawn`, which are.

3. **No filters.**
   - The service already filters in SQL by `tenantId`, `actorId` and `action` (console.service.ts:275-277; contract admin.ts:492-501).
   - The screen calls `admin.audit.list({ from, to, limit: 200 })` only (audit.tsx:46-48) and renders only the 30/60/90 Segments (:89-100).
   - Contracts carry no action vocabulary, so the app has nothing to build an action filter from.

4. **The distributor detail and the Support register name the requester differently** (api-probes-09 line 10 vs line 3).
   - `PlatformTenantsService.get` builds `supportGrants` with `toSupportGrant(g)` and no name (tenants.service.ts:138), so the default 'Distribution OS support' applies (support-grants.ts:27).
   - `admin.support.list` and `decorate` pass the looked-up name (support.service.ts:129, :206), as does the owner's `tenancy.support.list`.
   - The detail screen's InsidePanel never prints `requestedByName` (only app/support.tsx:151 and :254 do), so this half is an inconsistency in the `admin.tenants.get` reply, not a visible string on the detail page.

No second contributing cause: no trigger, RLS policy, offline path or worker job shapes the audit row, and Android and iOS render the same audit.tsx.

- `export type PlatformAuditAction = (typeof PLATFORM_AUDIT_ACTIONS)[number]`

Pure rules for one platform audit row. Type-only imports from @dos/contracts; no React, no @dos/ui.

- `auditWho(entry, word)` returns `entry.actorName ?? word(entry.actorRole)`.
- `auditReason(entry)` returns `after.reason` when it is a non-empty string, otherwise null.
- `auditChange(entry, fmt: { t, word, money })` returns `string | null` and reads the recorded payload defensively. Every branch returns null unless ALL the fields it prints are present with the right type, so it never throws and never prints 'undefined':
  - tenant.suspended / tenant.reactivated: `${word(from)} → ${word(to)}`
  - subscription.updated: `${side(from)} → ${side(after)}`, where `side` = `${word(plan)} · ${word(status)} · ${money(amountPaise)}`
  - subscription.created: `side(after)`
  - support.requested: `${word(scope)} · ${t('p8.hours', { hours })}`
  - support.withdrawn: `${word(was)} → ${word(now)}`
  - support.read: `${route} · ${word(outcome)}`
  - user.disabled: the `username`
  - tenant.onboarded: `${word(plan)} · ${t('p8.trialDays', { days: trialDays })}`
  - anything else: null

Only the stored words are translated. Money is formatted by the caller-supplied `money`; the helper does no arithmetic.

contractChange:
backend/libs/contracts/src/admin.ts has two changes.

1. **`PlatformAuditEntrySchema` gains `actorName: string | null` and `tenantName: string | null`.**
   - The addition is to the OUTPUT of `admin.audit.list` only, a GET. No idempotent reply stores it, so DOS-160 (stored replies re-validated against a newer contract) cannot trigger.
2. **New exports:** `PLATFORM_AUDIT_ACTIONS` and `PlatformAuditAction`.
   - They are the audit action vocabulary shared by the console's action chips and the five `platform_audit` writers (typed in module 13 and in `support-audit.interceptor.ts`).
   - No Zod schema uses them. `AdminAuditListInput.action` and the output `action` stay free strings.

**Why this cannot be avoided.**
- The name can only be resolved on the server: `users_visible` hides other administrators from a console session.
- The app cannot build the directory itself: a developer database holds 100+ platform users (docs/23 §10 row 13), and a closed account is not listed by `admin.users.list({ platformOnly })`.
- An action filter needs a vocabulary, and wire vocabulary lives only in contracts, so the app must not carry a second list.

**Unchanged:**
- `AuditEntrySchema` (tenancy) and `tenancy.audit.list`.
- The shape of `admin.tenants.get`. Only the VALUE of `supportGrants[].requestedByName` changes, from the placeholder to the real name.
- `PERMISSIONS` and `ADMIN_LEVELS`.

READMEs are regenerated with `pnpm docs:readme` in the lane before merge.
permissionsChange: none. `admin.audit.list` stays `PLATFORM` (permissions.ts:992), and in DOS-106's `ADMIN_LEVELS` both `admin.audit.list` and `admin.tenants.get` are open to every level (super, support, billing). No new procedure: the filters use existing `admin.audit.list` inputs, so the DOS-106 spec that probes every `admin.*` procedure is unaffected.
migration: none. `dos_support_requester_names(text[])` already exists from migration 0037: SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, EXECUTE granted to app_rw and app_worker, and a DO block that fails if the `platform_admins` join is ever dropped. It returns `users.name` for any id in `platform_admins`, including closed console accounts, so rows by a since-closed staff member stay named. Verified read-only on dos_qa: it resolves all 3 actors in `platform_audit`.

**WHAT I CHANGED (adversarial review, 2026-09-13):**

1. **Base moved.** DOS-106 is no longer "being implemented": it merged into main as 04c193e (e63ff17 + a89a9b1) while this review ran.
   - Every citation is re-pinned to 04c193e: `audit()` is now console.service.ts:263 with the mapper at :292-305, `toSupportGrant(g)` is tenants.service.ts:138, `requesterNames` is support.service.ts:221-232, `word.platform_admin` is strings.ts:380.
   - `requireActiveAdminLevel(tx, actorId, procedure)` (internals.ts:104) is already the first statement of `audit()` (:266) and `tenants.get()` (:118). The plan builds after those calls.
2. **Typing gap fixed.** The plan typed only `writePlatformAudit` and `insertPlatformAuditUnderSystem`.
   - `setStatus` passes `audit.action: string` (tenants.service.ts:315) into `writePlatformAudit` (:342), so the plan as written would not typecheck. That parameter is now typed.
   - The two literal writers now carry `satisfies PlatformAuditAction`: console.service.ts:182-184 (raw SQL 'user.disabled') and service/support-audit.interceptor.ts:74 ('support.read').
   - Without this, the plan's claim "the typed writer helpers enforce this" held for 3 of 5 writers, and DOS-107's enable would copy the untyped raw insert.
3. **Dropped the unused `PlatformAuditActionSchema` export.** Nothing validates with it, and an enum there invites wiring it into the output, which would 500 on dos_qa's rls.test fixture row `support.opened`.
4. **Spec reworked to the merged file.**
   - It uses the DOS-106 helpers `consoleHeaders`/`asConsole` (spec :817-833), not a raw `platformBearer`.
   - The colleague is a support-level account, so its row must be a `support.requested`: a suspension or plan change by it is now 403.
   - It states honestly that the tenantId/actorId/action narrowing assertions pass before the fix (the server filters exist). The red comes from `actorName`, `tenantName` and `requestedByName`.
   - It explains why DOS-106's `levelSnapshot(otherAdminUserId)` is not disturbed.
5. **Helper and test harden against partial payloads.** Every branch returns null unless the fields it prints are present, because dos_qa holds the fixture rows `support.requested {grantId}` and `support.opened {grantId}`. The last test now covers this.
6. **Verification corrected.**
   - The native Chips is a horizontal ScrollView (libs/ui/src/native/controls.tsx:355-360), so on Android the action chips scroll; they wrap only on web.
   - The detail page's InsidePanel never prints `requestedByName` (only app/support.tsx:151 and :254 do), so the step-4 check is API-level.
   - Added the lane build and README-regeneration rules from QA/STATE.md.
7. **audit.tsx details.**
   - The header comment (lines 1-10, "prints both rather than summarising them") is rewritten with the design.
   - The `before` panel branch is kept for a non-null `before` instead of being deleted.
   - The empty message switches back to `p8.empty` when no filter is set.

**CONFIRMED by reading the code and read-only SQL:**
- `users_visible` (schema/tenancy.ts:157-163) hides colleagues from a console session, so "join users" is wrong.
- The 0037 function is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, joins `platform_admins` with no `disabled_at` filter, is granted to app_rw, and resolves all 3 actors of the 23 rows on dos_qa.
- `support.approve` is written to the tenant `audit_log` (tenancy/support.service.ts:146-157), not `platform_audit`.
- `PLATFORM_AUDIT_ACTIONS` covers every production writer (9 actions, 5 writers). The helper reads all 9 payload shapes as the writers store them, including `from.status` 'trial' vs `status` 'trialing' and `was`/`now` values.
- `formatMoney` is exported by @dos/ui (shared.ts:19), and runtime imports from @dos/contracts are already used in admin-app src/lib/ui.tsx.
- `admin.audit.list` and `admin.tenants.get` are every-level reads in ADMIN_LEVELS.
- The app-level vitest precedents (3d64b94, 31af220) need no config file.
- No batch-2 plan in QA/evidence/batch2/plans touches these files.

**COULD NOT CONFIRM (read-only; nothing run):**
- That the two new core cases are red on main and green after.
- The exact lockfile delta.
- How the native Register lays out a long name in the 'chip' slot at 390 px: 'Anita Rao (Distribution OS support)' may truncate on the row. The Sheet shows it in full.

**RESIDUAL DOUBTS:**
- **Filter discoverability.** The person and distributorship filters are reached from a row, so "what did X do this month" needs one of X's rows in the window first. Alternatives considered and not chosen:
  - a kit `Search` picker over `admin.tenants.list({ q })`;
  - a staff chip row from `admin.users.list({ platformOnly })`, which costs extra reads, excludes closed accounts, and would list 100+ fixture admins on a developer database (dos_qa has 5).
  - Fable sign-off may prefer pickers; neither needs a contract change.
- **Withdrawal wording.** `word.rejected` = 'Refused' makes the console's withdrawal of an unanswered ask read "Waiting for their owner → Refused", as if the owner refused. That vocabulary is shared with the Support register and is not changed here (DOS-110 territory).
- **Adjacent, NOT fixed:**
  - a) The `audit()` keyset cursor compares `platform_audit.id < cursor` while ordering by `created_at`, and two raw writers use `gen_random_uuid()` v4 ids (console.service.ts:183, tenants.service.ts:389). Page 2 can skip or repeat rows. The screen does not page.
  - b) `entityType`/`entityId` are filtered in memory after LIMIT (console.service.ts:306-310), so a page can be short while `nextCursor` is non-null. This is the same query shape DOS-114 step 1 hits.
  - c) The stale word keys stay.
  - d) `platform_audit` records no level at action time, and today's level on a past row would mislead, so none is shown.
  - e) DOS-110 and DOS-111 are untouched.
